text.p: Giddings & Lewis Inc said Tuesday fourth-quarter bookings were $120.6 million, down from $154.0 million for the fourth quarter a year earlier.
Bookings for 1996 were $590.3 million, down from $663.6 million in 1995. The year-over-year reduction is attributable to a decline in bookings at Integrated Automation and in Europe.
Backlog as of December 31 was $208.3 million, a decline from $388.2 million at the end of 1995, the company said.

"We ended the year with leading technical capabilities and a strong balance sheet, with a debt-to-capitalization ratio of 22.6 percent," Joseph Coppola, chairman, said in a statement. "With this solid foundation, the resolution of customer concerns, the strengthening of European markets and the recent strengthening of markets for our large machine tools, we are confident that backlog levels will rebound."

Earlier, Giddings & Lewis, which supplies industrial automation products and machine tools, reported a net loss for the fourth quarter of $1.14 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.54 a share after a $30.3 million charge.
The fourth quarter 1996 loss included a pretax charge of $64.1 million for its Integrated Automation business, Giddings said. The charge was taken to improve operations and cut its workforce.
It also took $16.0 million in adjustments in the fourth quarter, including additional warranty expenses of $9.7 million and $6.3 million of costs to the write-down of inventory.

"We enter 1997 with a clean slate, and strong balance sheet," Coppola said. "Although it was painful in the short term, we did the right thing for the long-term future of the company. Giddings & Lewis recovered customer loyalty, which has been and always will be a top priority."

Fourth-quarter 1996 sales totaled $185.1 million, down from $208.9 million in the comparable quarter of 1995. This reflects a softness in demand for book-and-ship products and the impact of difficulties, which the company has addressed, in the Integrated Automation business, Giddings said.
